report:
## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by strong evidence.

Abaloparatide (Tymlos), an anabolic parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) analog, has been shown in high-quality randomized controlled trial data to significantly reduce vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

**Key evidence:**

1. **ACTIVE trial (pivotal Phase 3 RCT, JAMA 2016):** In this 18-month, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of over 2,400 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, subcutaneous abaloparatide significantly reduced the risk of new vertebral fractures (as well as nonvertebral fractures) compared with placebo (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27533157/?dopt=Abstract). Reported relative risk reductions for new vertebral fracture were on the order of 80-86% versus placebo.

2. **FDA prescribing information:** The FDA label confirms that TYMLOS "demonstrated consistent reductions in the risk of vertebral and nonvertebral fractures" regardless of age, prior fracture status, or baseline bone mineral density (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/208743s010lbl.pdf).

3. **Network meta-analysis (Osteoporosis International, 2019):** Pooled analysis comparing abaloparatide to placebo and other osteoporosis therapies confirmed abaloparatide "reduces the risk of fractures... versus placebo and compared with other treatment options" (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-019-04947-2).

4. **FRAX-based subgroup analysis (Archives of Osteoporosis, 2019):** Confirmed the effect held even in patients at increased fracture risk by FRAX probability, showing "significantly reduced the risk of vertebral and nonvertebral fractures" (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6373333/).

The extension study (ACTIVExtend) further showed durable fracture risk reduction when abaloparatide was followed by alendronate.

**Overall:** Multiple independent RCTs, regulatory review, and meta-analyses consistently support that abaloparatide significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. The claim is accurate.
